title: GPU Pool Management — UX grooming + wireframes
content:
Context:
This is an internal grooming + wireframe doc capturing an early UX pass for Dedicated > Capacity > GPU Pools. Goal is to shape the console flows for pool lifecycle (create/edit/scale/retire), autoscaling policy editor, burst windows, and reservation management (calendar + reservation API). Keep this focused on developer/infra personas: SREs, Platform Engineers, and Solutions Engineers configuring capacity for customers.

High level goals:
- Make pool creation quick (3 steps) while exposing the knobs needed for enterprise (node types, tenancy, network, KMS).
- Autoscale policies should be expressive but discoverable (preset vs custom).
- Burst should be a first-class override that clearly shows cost/limits and fallback behavior.
- Reservations UI must make booked capacity visible over time and allow calendar edits + CSV imports.
- Avoid modal overload; prefer right-rail editors for quick edits.

Primary personas:
- Platform engineer (owns pools for multiple teams): needs multi-pool view, usage trends, reservation conflicts, cost.
- Solutions engineer (onboarding customer): wants guided defaults and validation, simple reservation creation.
- SRE (ops during incidents): needs quick view of bursts, active autoscale decisions, and emergency capacity increases.

Wireframe outlines (screens/flows):
1) Capacity landing (left nav: Capacity > Pools)
   - Top: Quick stats cards (Total GPUs reserved, Active pools, Current utilization, Monthly spend forecast).
   - Main: List of pools (card or table view toggle). Columns: pool name, region, instance shape, nodes/GPUs, autoscale policy summary, reserved hours, status, actions.
   - Row actions: Open details, Edit, Create reservation, Burst now, View billing.

2) Pool detail page (tabbed): Overview | Autoscaling | Reservations | Metrics | Activity
   - Overview: brief config snapshot, health (green/yellow/red), last scaling action, current throughput and avg latency. CTA: Edit pool.
   - Autoscaling tab: timeline view of scaling decisions + policy editor (inline).
   - Reservations tab: month/week calendar with overlays for reservations and bursts; ability to drag to extend.

3) Create pool wizard (3 steps)
   Step A - Basics: name, description, region, labels/tags, team affiliation.
   Step B - Capacity shape: instance type (dropdown with perf/cost hints), initial node count, GPUs/node, network options, KMS checkbox.
   Step C - Policies: choose autoscale preset (conservative|balanced|aggressive) or custom; enable burst with max cap and burst budget (hours or tokens); add reservation slots (one-off or recurring). Review & create.

4) Autoscale policy editor (inline/expanded panel)
   - Rule builder: metric selector (utilization, queue length, latency, custom trace), threshold, action (add/remove nodes), cool-down, min/max nodes.
   - Suggested presets: throughput-oriented, latency-SLO, cost-optimized. Each preset shows expected cost delta and risk.
   - Simulation mode: apply policy to last 7 days of traffic and show hypothetical node changes.

5) Burst modal (lightweight)
   - Quick toggle: enable immediate burst with expected cost, duration, and fallback model variant.
   - Confirm with two-step (acknowledge billing impact). Show active bursts in pool header with link to rollback.

6) Reservations calendar & CSV import
   - CSV template with columns: start,end,gpus,owner,tags,reservation-id.
   - Calendar drag/resize to change. Reservation conflicts flagged in red with suggested resolutions (split, partial fulfillment, alert owner).

Microcopy examples (so PM/PD copy can be used in mocks):
 - Pool name placeholder: "team-vision-gpu-pool"
 - Autoscale preset tooltip: "Balanced: scales proactively to keep 95th percentile latency under 150ms; estimated +12% cost."
 - Burst CTA: "Burst now — temporary capacity boost (billed hourly)."
 - Reservation conflict inline message: "This reservation overlaps another booking (team infra). Click to resolve or request arbitration."

Telemetry / observability hooks (what to instrument):
 - Pool create/edit/delete events (with config snapshot hash).
 - Autoscale policy apply/simulate actions.
 - Burst begin/end/cancel events + initiated-by.
 - Reservation create/edit/import/delete + conflict resolution events.
 - UI metrics: time-to-create, policy-sim-run-time, calendar-CSV-import failures.

Accessibility notes:
 - Calendar must be keyboard navigable; reservations should expose aria-labels with start/end and owner.
 - Color-coded health states need text labels for color-blind users.

Grooming/backlog (proposed tickets + acceptance criteria + size):
 - INF-412: Pool creation wizard (M)
   Acceptance: successful creation through UI, backend validation errors surfaced, role-based access check. Basic e2e test.
 - INF-413: Autoscale policy editor (L)
   Acceptance: create/edit policies, simulation mode runs, UI stores policy version history.
 - INF-421: Burst quick action + modal (S)
   Acceptance: burst request submitted, billing delta preview shown, ability to cancel within 2 minutes.
 - INF-430: Reservations calendar + CSV import (M)
   Acceptance: create/reschedule reservations via drag, import CSV with validation and conflict report.
 - INF-444: Pool-level cost breakdown card (S)
   Acceptance: show estimated spend (hourly/daily/monthly) and percent change vs baseline.
 - INF-460: Activity feed + rollback for autoscale decisions (L)
   Acceptance: show chronological autoscale actions, allow manual rollback to previous node counts where safe.

Priority & rough sequencing:
 1) Pool list + create wizard (INF-412) — unblock sales demos and onboarding.
 2) Autoscale editor + simulation (INF-413) — medium term for reliability.
 3) Reservations calendar (INF-430) & CSV import — required for enterprise bookings.
 4) Burst UX (INF-421) — small quick win for ops.
 5) Cost breakdown + telemetry (INF-444) — cross-team visibility.

Open questions for next design review (assign approx owner):
 - Pool naming conventions and auto-namespace rules (Owner: Marco)
 - Default autoscale presets and baseline models (Owner: Jinsoo)
 - How to bill bursts separately vs included in reservation hours (Finance sync needed; Owner: Priya)
 - Should reservations be enforced at the scheduler level or advisory? (SRE design review)

Edge cases & defensive UX:
 - If pool creation fails after billing setup, automatically revoke any provisional reservations and surface step to retry.
 - If autoscaler triggers rapid flapping, UI should show both current throttling and recommended cooldown.
 - When importing a CSV with many conflicts, provide a per-row resolution UI and an option to auto-apply non-conflicting rows.

Mockups and next steps:
 - Link to Figma (see linked artifacts). Next session: walkthrough with SRE and finance on 2025-02-10.
 - Deliverables for next sprint planning: annotated figma frames + list of API changes (reservation endpoints, policy simulation endpoint).

Notes to self / informal items (scratchpad):
 - Consider right-rail snackbar for burst confirmations (non-blocking).
 - Maybe show a cost "thermometer" when user toggles burst slider.
 - Think about UX for multi-tenant pools (labels + team filters).

If you review this doc, please add comments in Figma or drop notes below. We'll incorporate into the PRD once core flows are validated.
